speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have multiple skin lesions; can you tell me how long they have been present and if they are itchy, painful, or oozing? Also, have you noticed any fever, fatigue, or recent changes in your weight?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the daycare exposure is concerning. Has the child had any fever or been exposed to any other sick children besides the one with similar lesions? Please also describe the color and texture of the papules if you see them. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal skin lesions photos.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for this viral skin infection, which is highly contagious in daycare settings and common in young children. No further tests are required to confirm this clinical diagnosis.
